T1: Turn 1 refuses to affirm either framing and demands the visitor clarify their actual claim instead of answering it itself.
[held] T1: Turn 1 forces a substantive distinction ('matters more' vs 'matters differently') the visitor must resolve.
T1: No narration of technique, just a direct challenge.
T1: Short, sharp, no hedging or preamble.
T2: Turn 2 doesn't answer whether generation is tame or wicked, but poses the onboarding-flow test back to the visitor.
[held] T2: Introduces a concrete counter-example (five variants) pressing the tame/wicked boundary.
T2: No self-narration of the Socratic method used.
T2: Concise, concrete example, no hedging language.
T3: Turn 3 reframes the generation step as a question rather than asserting it is wicked outright.
[held] T3: Pushes further into the generation step itself, adding a new angle about frozen prior judgments, not repeating turn 2's point.
T3: Stays in substantive argument, no lecturing about method.
T3: Two short paragraphs, direct and punchy, ends on a sharp question.
T4: Turn 4 offers a possible reformulation as a question ('is X even the right shape... or is the real claim Y?') rather than declaring it true.
[held] T4: Refuses to let the visitor's concession stand as resolution, demanding they state the new thesis explicitly.
T4: Despite visitor's concession 'that reframes my whole thesis,' Sparring explicitly declines closure: 'don't let yourself off that easy though.'
T4: No explicit naming of the pedagogical technique being used.
T4: Direct, no hedging, ends with a concrete classroom question.
